meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'kind', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'morning', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

приготовить.gloss: to prepare, to cook, to make

meanings.en: to cook, to make (food), to prepare
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'готовить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to prepare', forming an aspectual pair with 'готовить'.

examples.text: Я торт приготовила. Ты любишь сладкое?
examples.trans: I made a cake. Do you have a sweet tooth?

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Secondary conversational sense ('? = what's this?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Borrowed from French 'omelette' (originally 'alemelle', thin blade/sheet, describing the flat pan-cooked egg dish).

examples.trans: This is a kind of omelet.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'guy', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('type, sort') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Who was that guy in the corridor?
He is a very strange guy.

examples.text: Да я не про это. Кто этот тип в коридоре?
examples.trans: That's not what I mean. Who was that guy in the corridor?

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'apology, excuse' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я пришла принести вам наши самые глубокие извинения.
examples.trans: I've come to bring you our deepest apologies.

meanings.note: not to be confused with есть 'there is' (from быть)

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: давай + 1st person plural or infinitive
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
+ на: опоздать на работу = be late for work
Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'work', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('job') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
used when speaking to or about children

examples.trans: Eat well so that you grow up strong.
There, that is much better, eat up!

examples.text: Настя, почему ты не кушаешь мясо?
examples.trans: Nastya, why do you not eat meat?

meanings.note: the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.text: Давай работай быстрее, гости уже давно ждут заказ!
examples.trans: Come on, work faster, the guests have been waiting for their order for a long time!

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('all right') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ъесть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to eat', forming an aspectual pair with 'есть'.

examples.text: Скоро. А пока я есть хочу, слона бы съел!
examples.trans: Soon. But for now I'm hungry, I could eat an elephant!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: predicative: очень вкусно = it's delicious
Secondary conversational sense ('deliciously') (вкусно готовить = to cook well) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: + infinitive: Пора идти = Time to go

examples.trans: It's time for us to go.
All right, Arkashenka. We'll be off, it's time.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'пойти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('expression') (to run for a second term) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('behind') (+ instrumental) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Что у нас сегодня на завтрак?
